title: EATING BREAD IN THE PRESENCE OF GOD

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Then Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, brought a burnt offering and other sacrifices
to God, and Aaron came with all the elders of Israel to eat a meal with Moses'
father-in-law in the presence of God." - Ex 18:12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Look at who is at this table. Aaron, the high priest. All the elders of Israel.
And Jethro, a Midianite, who has just brought offerings to the LORD.

They eat together "in the presence of God."

This is a striking picture so early in Israel's story. A man from outside the
covenant people worships the LORD, and Israel's leadership sits down and eats
with him. There is no suggestion that this was improper.

Notice that Jethro brings the offering. He is not a spectator at someone else's
worship; he participates. And notice that the meal is described as being in
God's presence, which makes it more than a social occasion.

This anticipates something that will unfold across the whole Bible. God's
purposes were never limited to one ethnic group. Peter, centuries later, would
need a vision from heaven before he was willing to eat with Cornelius, and his
conclusion was: "I now realize how true it is that God does not show favoritism"
(Acts 10:34).

Shared meals matter more than we think. Much of Jesus' ministry happened at
tables, and He was criticised for who He ate with.

Who is at your table?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Who would feel genuinely welcome at your table?
2. Is there someone you have quietly kept at a distance?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that Your welcome has always been wider than we expect. Make
my table an open one. Amen.
